DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon).

The combination of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth, and abdominal distension in an infant is highly suggestive of this condition. The abdominal X-ray and ultrasound requested previously will confirm intestinal obstruction and gas pattern consistency. If these results are equivocal, a contrast enema and rectal biopsy will be required for definitive confirmation.
